# Estuarine 'Omics & Microbial Ecology
**Joseph H. Vineis, PhD** — Investigating microbial genomes at the molecular level to understand how sediment and water-column communities drive coastal biogeochemistry.

[Explore Research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-light .btn-lg .mt-2}

## Core Research Pillars

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.research-card}
### Methane Cycling Microbial Consortia
Examining decomposers, methanogenic and methanotrophic communities across brackish marshes (*Typha angustifolia*) to resolve how microbial decomposition regulates greenhouse gas fluxes.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.research-card}
### Salt Marsh Sediment Biogeochemistry
Using metagenomics and metatranscriptomics across depth and nutrient gradients to uncover metabolic handoffs, nitrogen transformations, and carbon storage.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.research-card}
### Genome-Resolved 'Omics & Cultivation
Combining high-resolution bioinformatics, pangenomics, and targeted microbial cultivation to link genomic potential with physiological activity.
:::
:::

:::

## About

I am a microbial ecologist and scientific informatics researcher studying how microbial communities shape elemental cycling in dynamic coastal ecosystems. My work integrates genome-resolved metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and physiological experiments across salt marshes, brackish wetlands, and coastal waters.
